issues.legal_issue: The characteristics that bring a building within a statutory exemption are assessed when the applicability of the rent-control law is in issue, rather than only on the law’s commencement date.
material_facts: The building had previously been let as a building simpliciter and was treated as subject to the rent-control law.
After recovering possession, the owners renovated and equipped the building for use as a cinema and arranged to lease it with the cinema equipment.
issues.conclusion: An exemption can apply when the relevant qualifying characteristics arise after the rent-control law commenced; it is not confined to buildings that had those characteristics on the commencement date.
issues.legal_principle: Section 2(1) lists exempt classes of buildings, and the building must possess the relevant character when the law is sought to be applied to it. The Court relied on the language and scheme of section 2(1), including its different ownership- and use-based exemptions; it cited no earlier cases.

predicates.rent_control_exemption_dispute: The proceeding concerns whether a building is covered by a rent-control law or falls within an exemption from it.
predicates.qualifying_characteristics_exist_when_co: The building has the characteristics specified for an exemption when its coverage is being assessed.

issues.definition: When a rent-control exemption dispute concerns a building with qualifying characteristics at the time coverage is assessed, its exemption status tracks those characteristics at that assessment.

issues.legal_issue: A building previously subject to rent control may become exempt upon a vacancy when the owner intends to lease it for a specified industrial or entertainment use together with the plant and apparatus needed for that use.
material_facts: The building had been let to earlier tenants as a building simpliciter and was treated as subject to the Act when they vacated it.
The owners renovated the premises and installed cinema equipment, furniture and fittings.
The owners agreed to lease the premises as a fully equipped cinema, and the lease documents and cinema-licence proceedings supported that intended use and manner of letting.
issues.conclusion: The building fell within the exemption for a cinema leased with its plant and apparatus, so the rent-control law ceased to apply even though the building had previously been covered and the later letting had not been preceded by an allotment order.
issues.legal_principle: Section 2(1)(d) covers a building used or intended to be used as a cinema or theatre where the plant and apparatus installed for that purpose is leased with the building. Read as a whole, the provision does not require a prior valid subsisting lease of the equipped premises: the landlord’s intention to put the building to the specified use and to let it with the necessary plant and apparatus is sufficient. Sections 11, 13 and 16 apply to buildings that remain within the Act; section 2(1)(d) may exclude a building from the Act. The Court cited no earlier cases.

rule.if: rent_control_vacancy_allotment_proceeding and vacancy_occurs and owner_intends_specified_cinema_use and owner_intends_lease_with_necessary_equipment

predicates.rent_control_vacancy_allotment_proceedin: The proceeding concerns whether a vacant building may be dealt with under a rent-control allotment scheme.
predicates.vacancy_occurs: The building becomes vacant after being occupied by a tenant.
predicates.owner_intends_specified_cinema_use: The owner intends the building to be used as a cinema or theatre.
predicates.owner_intends_lease_with_necessary_equip: The owner intends to lease the building together with the plant and apparatus needed for that use.

issues.definition: In a rent-control vacancy-allotment proceeding, a vacancy combined with the owner’s intended cinema use and intended lease of the necessary equipment means the building is excluded from the allotment scheme.

issues.legal_issue: The authority responsible for rent-control allotments determines whether a building is covered by the law, after hearing the landlord, and need not hear prospective allottees on that coverage question.
material_facts: The owners claimed that the building was exempt because they intended to lease it as a fully equipped cinema.
An applicant sought allotment and asked that the coverage issue be reconsidered with his participation.

The Court held that an allotment application gives its maker only a right to be considered for a building to which the law applies, not a right in any particular property before coverage is determined.
issues.conclusion: The competent authority must decide the building’s coverage on the materials and any inspection or inquiry it considers necessary, after hearing the landlord; it should not permit prospective allottees to intervene in that determination.
issues.legal_principle: Under the scheme of the Act, the District Magistrate deals with buildings to which the Act applies and determines whether a building is available for allotment. Sections 15 to 17 govern vacancy notification, allotment and release, while section 2(1) defines exemptions. An allotment applicant has no property-specific right until the authority determines that the building is one it may allot. The Court cited no earlier cases.

rule.if: rent_control_vacancy_allotment_proceeding and coverage_question_precedes_allotment and landlord_claims_exemption and applicant_seeks_to_intervene

predicates.rent_control_vacancy_allotment_proceedin: The proceeding concerns whether a vacant building may be allotted under a rent-control scheme.
predicates.coverage_question_precedes_allotment: The authority must determine whether the building is covered before deciding whether it may allot the building.
predicates.landlord_claims_exemption: The landlord asserts that the building is outside the rent-control scheme.
predicates.applicant_seeks_to_intervene: A person seeking an allotment asks to participate in the determination of the building’s coverage.

issues.definition: When coverage must be decided before allotment and the landlord claims an exemption, the authority decides that issue after hearing the landlord, not prospective allottees seeking to intervene.

issues.legal_issue: A person who has only applied for allotment has no standing, on that basis alone, to challenge a cinema licence granted to another occupier.
material_facts: The challenger had applied to have the building allotted to him.
The other proposed occupiers obtained a cinema licence for the premises.
The challenger had no established right to occupy the building, and his allotment application did not itself confer a right in the property.
issues.conclusion: The challenger lacked locus standi to challenge the grant of the cinema licence merely because he had sought allotment of the building.
issues.legal_principle: An application for allotment confers only a right to be considered for a building that is subject to the Act; it confers no right in a particular property until the competent authority determines that the building is covered. Section 13 also makes a right to exhibit cinema shows in the premises a condition relevant to lawful occupation and licensing. The Court cited no earlier cases.

predicates.challenge_to_cinema_license: The proceeding challenges a licence to operate a cinema in a building.
predicates.challenger_has_only_allotment_applicatio: The challenger has sought allotment but has not obtained an allotment or other right to occupy the building.
predicates.challenger_has_no_established_right_to_o: The challenger has no independently established right to occupy the premises.

issues.definition: A person challenging a cinema licence lacks standing when the person has only applied for allotment and has no established right to occupy the building.

issues.legal_issue: A remand for renewed consideration of allotment is unnecessary when the record clearly establishes that the owner intends to lease the building as a fully equipped cinema and the building is therefore exempt.
material_facts: The authority declared the building vacant and proceeded toward allotment.
An inspection report described the premises as a fully equipped cinema and indicated that the owners had let it to the proposed cinema operators.
The lease agreement, registered lease, inspection report and cinema-licence application and grant supported the owners’ intention to lease the premises as a fully equipped cinema.
issues.conclusion: The matter did not need to be remanded for a fresh determination; the evidence established the exempt intended use and letting, leaving the authority without jurisdiction to proceed with allotment.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 2(1)(d), a building intended for cinema use and intended to be leased with the necessary plant and apparatus is exempt. The authority may determine coverage on the available materials, but a prospective allottee has no right to intervene in that determination. The Court applied these principles to the record and cited no earlier cases.

predicates.appeal_from_vacancy_or_allotment_decisio: The proceeding challenges a decision declaring a building vacant or allowing it to proceed toward allotment.
predicates.record_clearly_shows_intended_cinema_lea: The evidence clearly shows that the owner intends to lease the building as a cinema with the necessary equipment.

issues.definition: In an appeal from a vacancy or allotment decision, a record clearly showing an intended equipped-cinema lease makes remand unnecessary and prevents allotment from proceeding.
